Jordan — 2:30pm ET on Wed Aug 19 works for us. I’ll update the invite to 2:30–3:45pm ET and include a short run-of-show.

To answer your Hosted vs Dedicated question pre-call (high level):
- Hosted (fastest path):
  - Pros: zero infra setup, flexible short-term quota bumps, predictable per-token billing
  - Cons: concurrency capped by quota; for sustained high QPS you may see throttling without a Dedicated commit
  - Suggested initial settings for your profile (30 concurrent, 1.5k avg, 3k burst): request Hosted quota bump to allow ~120 requests/min and a token budget of ~6M tokens/day for the trial window. Default soft limits may be lower — we’ll file the quota request as part of the kickoff.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity):
  - Pros: predictable throughput, consistent latency, isolation for compliance
  - Cons: commit required, longer lead time to provision in some regions
  - Suggested baseline: 1 x T4-equivalent pool to support sustained 30 concurrent at your token sizes with headroom for spikes; we’ll run perf profiling during the POC to refine.

Rate limits & load testing notes:
- Start with a 10-minute ramp (10% -> 100% QPS) to validate KV/prefix caching behavior and network stability.
- For burst tolerance, test 5s spikes at 150% QPS — we expect Hosted to absorb short bursts if quota bump is approved.
- We’ll run a scripted load test (attached plan) and capture latency percentiles, token counts, and failed requests.

Prep for the call: please drop the representative prompts into the POC worksheet and confirm who will run the load test (we’ll need their email to share the script). I’ve attached the load_test_plan.md and will send an updated calendar invite (invite.ics) in a follow-up.

Attachments: load_test_plan.md, POC-worksheet.xlsx (updated).

See you Wed 2:30pm ET — Priya
